description: Palace is Helsinki's benchmark luxury restaurant: a 10th-floor dining room above the South Harbour with the strongest combination of history, views, service and culinary ambition in Finland. Chef Eero Vottonen's kitchen reads Finnish nature through a highly polished modern Nordic lens, with Japanese inflections and one of the country's most serious wine programs. For an affluent visitor, it is the clearest first fine-dining booking in the city.
highlights: Two Michelin stars, harbour panorama, 1952 Olympic-era landmark building and Finland's most prestigious fine-dining address.
sources: Michelin Guide; Palace; MyHelsinki; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland; 50Best Discovery

description: Grön is Helsinki's most distinctive small-room fine-dining restaurant, built around vegetables, wild plants, ferments and a restrained Nordic sensibility. The room is intimate and relaxed, but the cooking has the clarity and confidence expected of a serious two-star address. It is the counterpoint to Palace: quieter, earthier and more ingredient-led, yet every bit a destination dinner.
highlights: Two Michelin stars, plant-forward creative cooking, chef-served tasting menu and strong sustainability identity.
sources: Michelin Guide; Grön; MyHelsinki; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland; Helsinki Times

description: Olo is one of Helsinki's defining modern Nordic restaurants, combining long-running Michelin credibility with a polished but unforced dining room near the Market Square. The kitchen works with northern ingredients, clear flavors and a contemporary sense of rhythm rather than heavy formality. It remains a high-confidence choice for a special dinner that feels elegant, Finnish and approachable.
highlights: Michelin-starred modern Nordic restaurant by the Market Square with high-quality wines and warm service.
sources: Michelin Guide; Olo; MyHelsinki; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland

description: Demo is Helsinki's long-serving Michelin survivor, now recast high above Ruoholahti in a dramatic 14th-floor dining room. The move has given the restaurant a more architectural, city-view identity while preserving the chef's-menu format and technical confidence that made it important in the first place. It is a strong choice for diners who want classic fine-dining discipline with a contemporary Helsinki skyline setting.
highlights: Michelin star since 2007, new Ruoholahti sky-level location and a 175-euro chef's menu.
sources: Michelin Guide; Demo; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland; SuomiGuide

description: Finnjävel Salonki turns Finnish culinary heritage into a refined, highly designed fine-dining experience beside Kunsthalle Helsinki. Traditional ingredients, preservation techniques and nostalgic flavors are reworked with enough precision and theatre to feel special rather than folkloric. It is one of the best restaurants in the city for visitors who want fine dining that could only be in Finland.
highlights: Michelin-starred Finnish heritage cuisine, Nordic design setting and detailed modern interpretations of traditional dishes.
sources: Michelin Guide; Finnjävel; MyHelsinki; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland

description: Boreal is the new-generation Helsinki fine-dining address that moved fastest into the city's top tier. The restaurant works with foraging, fermentation, regenerative farming and Finnish seasons, but the experience is composed and adult rather than rustic. Its 2026 Michelin star makes it one of the most important current openings for diners tracking the city's future.
highlights: New 2026 Michelin star, Design District location, wild-foraged ingredients and fermentation-led Nordic cooking.
sources: Michelin Guide; Boreal; MyHelsinki; Time Out; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland

description: Baskeri & Basso, usually shortened to BasBas, is the city's most important high-end bistro and a perennial Helsinki insider favorite. The room is informal, warm and wine-driven, but the ingredient quality and consistency put it firmly in the same conversation as more formal restaurants. It is exactly the kind of place a Michelin diner might choose on a night when atmosphere and pleasure matter more than ceremony.
highlights: Finland 50 Best runner-up, natural-wine culture, courtyard bistro atmosphere and ingredient-led sharing dishes.
sources: Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland; Helsinki Times; MyHelsinki; BasBas

description: Jason is the independent restaurant from Michelin-awarded chef Jari Vesivalo and one of Helsinki's strongest recent high-end openings. The cooking is precise but relaxed, with vegetables, seafood and game treated with the care of a fine-dining kitchen. It belongs high on the list because it has already become a serious local industry signal rather than just a newcomer with buzz.
highlights: Michelin-awarded chef ownership, strong 2026 Finland 50 Best ranking and polished but low-threshold set-menu dining.
sources: Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland; MyHelsinki; Jason; Monocle

description: Savoy is Helsinki's grandest classic restaurant, an Alvar and Aino Aalto-designed dining room overlooking Esplanade Park. Chef Patron Helena Puolakka keeps the Finnish-French cooking seasonal and contemporary without compromising the room's old-world elegance. Its history, wine cellar, terrace and service make it a luxury landmark even without a current Michelin star.
highlights: Aalto-designed Helsinki landmark, Finnish-French cooking, Esplanade views and one of Finland's largest wine cellars.
sources: Michelin Guide; Savoy; MyHelsinki; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland

description: Alexanderplats gives Helsinki a proper polished brasserie on one of the city's most visible civic addresses. The cooking is clear, elegant and European, with the kind of all-evening service rhythm that works for business dinners, regulars and visiting guests alike. It earns its place as a luxury-adjacent alternative to the city's tasting menus.
highlights: High-ranking Helsinki brasserie on Eteläesplanadi with European classics, terrace energy and a strong wine-and-beer program.
sources: Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland; Alexanderplats; MyHelsinki; TableOnline

description: Luovuus kukkii kaaoksesta is a small, intense Kaartinkaupunki restaurant with a particular talent for raw-aged fish, seafood, sake and wine. The cooking feels personal and unstandardized, but the experience is serious enough for guests who normally book Michelin-level restaurants. It brings a sharper, more modern seafood-and-drinks voice to Helsinki's high-end core.
highlights: Intimate seafood-focused room with raw-aged fish, sake, cocktails, wines and one of Helsinki's strongest local rankings.
sources: Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland; Luovuus kukkii kaaoksesta; MyHelsinki; Time Out

description: Vinkkeli is a polished classic restaurant and wine room in Kaartinkaupunki, balancing old-fashioned virtues with a fresh local following. The kitchen is direct and confident, the service is personable, and the wine selection is treated as seriously as the food. It is one of Helsinki's most reliable high-end-casual choices for diners who prefer timelessness over novelty.
highlights: Michelin-selected classic restaurant with attentive service, historical setting and a strong wine-led identity.
sources: Michelin Guide; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland; Vinkkeli; MyHelsinki

description: Bona Fide is a small Kruununhaka bistro that shows why Helsinki's less formal restaurants can still matter to serious diners. Its seasonal menus are compact, modern and produce-led, with an upbeat room and a confident sense of value. The Michelin Bib Gourmand signal is useful, but the restaurant's appeal is really its precision, warmth and neighborhood energy.
highlights: Michelin Bib Gourmand, compact modern menus, Kruununhaka bistro setting and relaxed but serious service.
sources: Michelin Guide; Bona Fide; MyHelsinki; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland

description: Teller has quickly become one of Helsinki's most interesting new high-end neighborhood restaurants. It brings a warm, slightly radical personality to classic dinner formats, with thoughtful wines and service that feels personal rather than scripted. For a well-traveled guest, it offers the pleasures of a local dining room while still clearing the affluent-dinner bar.
highlights: Highly ranked new Töölö restaurant with story-led hospitality, polished bistro cooking and European wines.
sources: Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland; Teller; MyHelsinki; TableOnline

description: Café Savoy is the more relaxed sister to Savoy, but it still occupies a serious place in the city's affluent dining landscape. Southern French inspiration, Esplanade address and Financier Group polish make it feel like a grown-up brasserie rather than a casual cafe. It is a strong choice when the brief is beautiful, central and less formal than a tasting menu.
highlights: Southern French brasserie cooking on Eteläesplanadi from the Savoy orbit, with polished service and central luxury appeal.
sources: Michelin Guide; Café Savoy; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland; MyHelsinki

description: Kuurna is a small Kruununhaka restaurant with the longevity and local affection that make a simple room feel like an institution. The menu changes regularly, ingredients are carefully sourced and the tone is intimate rather than showy. It belongs here because it gives sophisticated diners a high-quality Helsinki evening without the formality of the city's starriest rooms.
highlights: Michelin-selected Kruununhaka classic with seasonal Finnish cooking, small-producer ingredients and an intimate bistro mood.
sources: Michelin Guide; Kuurna; MyHelsinki; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland

description: Shii is Helsinki's most compelling intimate Japanese counter, a hidden 15-seat omakase and otsumami room in the city centre. The format is small, ritualized and product-driven, supported by a notably curated sake, wine and whisky selection. It adds a precise Japanese fine-dining option to a city whose top restaurants are otherwise dominated by Nordic idioms.
highlights: Hidden 15-seat omakase counter, Michelin selection, sake and whisky pairings and a top-20 Finnish restaurant ranking.
sources: Michelin Guide; Shii; MyHelsinki; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland; Falstaff

description: Nolla's zero-waste philosophy is more than branding: it shapes the sourcing, menu design, drinks list and rhythm of the restaurant. The result is relaxed, seasonal and modern without losing the seriousness required for a dinner-focused booking. It is one of Helsinki's clearest sustainability stories for affluent diners who still want good service, wine and a full evening meal.
highlights: Michelin Bib Gourmand, zero-waste philosophy, seasonal local ingredients and sustainable wines in Punavuori.
sources: Michelin Guide; Nolla; MyHelsinki; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland

description: Nokka is a long-running Katajanokka waterfront restaurant whose identity is built around Finnish producers, wild ingredients and responsible sourcing. Its old warehouse setting gives the meal a strong sense of place, especially for visitors who want the harbour rather than a downtown dining room. It remains a very relevant high-end alternative because it combines local sourcing, wine and a classic Helsinki waterside atmosphere.
highlights: Michelin-selected harbour restaurant in an old warehouse, known for Finnish farmers, wild ingredients and sustainable sourcing.
sources: Michelin Guide; Nokka; MyHelsinki; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland

description: Latitude 25 is Finland's pioneer omakase restaurant and remains one of Helsinki's most serious seafood counters. The format is reservation-led, small and precise, with a strong emphasis on raw and cooked seafood prepared directly in front of guests. It is an important inclusion for affluent diners looking for Japanese discipline rather than Nordic tasting-menu language.
highlights: Finland's first omakase restaurant, Michelin selection, seafood-led counter dining and strict reservation-only format.
sources: Michelin Guide; Latitude 25; MyHelsinki; Falstaff

description: Natura is a casual fine-dining restaurant in the Design District that translates Finnish nature into a polished but relaxed tasting-menu experience. Fermentation, pickling, smoking and chargrilling appear throughout the kitchen's seasonal language, while the room stays small and warm. It is a strong bridge between Helsinki's Michelin world and its more informal chef-driven bistros.
highlights: Michelin-selected casual fine dining with Finnish ingredients, fermentation, open-kitchen intimacy and sustainable menu thinking.
sources: Michelin Guide; Natura; MyHelsinki; official restaurant website

description: Bistro Bardot is the city's most polished modern French bistro-brasserie, occupying a handsome central room in Kluuvi. It is lively and social, but the raw bar, seasonal kitchen and quality of ingredients give it dinner credibility beyond scene value. For affluent diners who want seafood, champagne and French comfort without a tasting menu, it is an obvious Helsinki booking.
highlights: Michelin-selected French bistro-brasserie with raw bar, historical interiors, cocktails and central social energy.
sources: Michelin Guide; Bistro Bardot; MyHelsinki; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland

description: Restaurant 305 has become one of Helsinki's most credible new relaxed restaurants, combining a Hakaniemi neighborhood feeling with stronger culinary ambition than the label suggests. The kitchen rethinks Finnish classics with modern technique, while natural wines, cocktails and the old three-storey building give the evening a distinctive identity. Its Michelin Bib Gourmand confirms quality, but the broader appeal is smart, grown-up and current.
highlights: Michelin Bib Gourmand, Hakaniemi heritage building, natural wines, cocktails and modern Finnish bistro cooking.
sources: Michelin Guide; Restaurant 305; MyHelsinki; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland

description: Muru is a Helsinki bistro classic built around daily ingredients, relaxed service and one of the city's most serious wine cultures. The room is small and charming, with a confidence that comes from long-term local affection rather than hype. It is a natural choice for diners who want a bottle-led evening with excellent food in a less formal register.
highlights: Michelin-selected wine bistro, Helsinki classic since 2010 and known for sommelier-led pairings and warm service.
sources: Michelin Guide; Muru; MyHelsinki; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland

description: Boulevard Bar & Seafood is Helsinki's most relevant upscale seafood-and-shellfish room for diners who want a proper dinner rather than a tasting menu. The kitchen leans on classic technique and good fish, while the Bulevardi address keeps the experience central and social. It fills an important niche in the city: polished seafood with an adult, affluent crowd.
highlights: Michelin-selected seafood restaurant on Bulevardi with shellfish, classic fish cooking and polished social energy.
sources: Michelin Guide; Boulevard Bar & Seafood; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland; MyHelsinki

description: plein is a Vallila neighborhood restaurant with a much larger reputation than its modest room suggests. The seasonal menu is concise, creative and wine-friendly, and its Puu-Vallila setting gives affluent visitors a different texture of Helsinki than the central luxury corridors. It is a local-critical favorite that still works for serious destination dining.
highlights: Michelin-selected Vallila bistro, Time Out Helsinki favorite, seasonal menu and relaxed but expert service.
sources: Michelin Guide; plein; Time Out; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland

description: Le Ankka gives Ullanlinna a compact, characterful restaurant built around French cooking, Finnish ingredients and a moody design language. The open-kitchen energy and small scale keep it lively, while the cooking and wines are serious enough for a destination dinner. It is one of Helsinki's strongest new-wave neighborhood bistros for affluent diners who enjoy charm and craft in equal measure.
highlights: Michelin-selected French-Finnish bistro on Huvilakatu with open kitchen, intimate scale and strong local sourcing.
sources: Michelin Guide; Le Ankka; MyHelsinki; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland

description: The Grand Bar & Grill is Helsinki's strongest premium grill candidate, set in the historic Grand Residence 21 building. The focus on high-quality Finnish meat and classic dishes gives the city an affluent steak-and-grill option that is not just a chain-format steakhouse. It is a useful booking for business dinners and guests who want substance, polish and a slightly grander room.
highlights: Historic Grand Residence 21 setting, Finnish meat, classic grill cooking and a strong 2026 local ranking.
sources: Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland; The Grand Bar & Grill; MyHelsinki; TableOnline

description: BISOUBISOU brings a rare rooftop-restaurant dimension to Helsinki, with a 24th-floor Kalasatama setting, glass terrace and French brasserie energy. Its appeal is more social and scenic than Michelin-like, but the food offer and local ranking make it credible as an affluent dinner venue. It is the city's clearest skyline-view restaurant for guests who want design, height and atmosphere.
highlights: 24th-floor rooftop brasserie in Kalasatama with French-New York attitude, glass terrace and city views.
sources: Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland; BISOUBISOU; MyHelsinki; The Rooftop Guide

description: Gaijin remains Helsinki's most established upscale Asian social restaurant, combining dark contemporary design with Japanese, Korean and northern Chinese references. The sharing format, tasting menus and attentive service make it more dinner-focused than a fashionable bar-restaurant. It rounds out the high-end core by adding a polished Asian alternative on the same Bulevardi address as several serious restaurants.
highlights: Michelin-selected Asian restaurant with dark contemporary decor, sharing menus and buzzing Bulevardi atmosphere.
sources: Michelin Guide; Gaijin; MyHelsinki; official restaurant website

description: Kosmos is one of Helsinki's great old restaurant rooms, a family-run classic that has been part of the city's culinary culture since 1924. The interior, art and menu of blini, Baltic herring, Vorschmack and other classics give sophisticated visitors a direct route into local dining memory. It is informal compared with the fine-dining core, but it is culturally essential and still a proper sit-down dinner.
highlights: Family-run Helsinki classic since 1924 with original dining-room character, Finnish-European dishes and artist-restaurant heritage.
sources: Kosmos; MyHelsinki; World of Mouth; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland

description: Sea Horse, affectionately known as Sikala, is the kind of old Helsinki restaurant locals mention with real feeling. Since 1933 it has served traditional Finnish food in Ullanlinna with generous portions, vintage interiors and a room full of civic memory. It is exactly the right relaxed-night counterweight to the city's modern Nordic fine dining.
highlights: Legendary Ullanlinna restaurant since 1933, loved for traditional Finnish dishes, vintage atmosphere and local regulars.
sources: Sea Horse; MyHelsinki; World of Mouth; local classic restaurant guides

description: Carelia is a brasserie opposite the Finnish National Opera, set in an old pharmacy interior with a mood that feels part Paris, part Helsinki and part historic Viipuri. The menu leans on French classics, good ingredients and a deep wine culture rather than culinary fireworks. It is a credible informal favorite for affluent diners who appreciate atmosphere, heritage and a grown-up room.
highlights: Historic old-pharmacy brasserie by the National Opera with French classics, original decor and a broad wine program.
sources: Carelia; MyHelsinki; Visit Finland; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland

description: Lehtovaara is one of Helsinki's enduring classic restaurants, known for high-quality Finnish and international cooking across generations. Its Taka-Töölö location and glass terrace give it a neighborhood-luxury feel rather than touristy obviousness. For a relaxed local dinner, it offers exactly the sort of old-school confidence that sophisticated visitors often appreciate.
highlights: Longstanding Taka-Töölö classic with Finnish and international dishes, terrace dining and old-school hospitality.
sources: Lehtovaara; MyHelsinki; local classic restaurant guides; Viisi Tähteä 50 Best Restaurants Finland

description: Kolme Kruunua is a preserved 1950s Kruununhaka classic serving meatballs, pyttipannu, fried Baltic herring and other Finnish staples with deep local recognition. It is not a luxury restaurant, but it is a proper dinner room with a cultural role that an informed visitor can understand immediately. The inclusion protects Helsinki's old dining identity alongside the modern fine-dining scene.
highlights: Legendary Kruununhaka classic from 1952 with preserved interiors, Finnish comfort dishes and strong local affection.
sources: Kolme Kruunua; MyHelsinki; World of Mouth; local classic restaurant guides
